About Rimstone

Led by Tim Perrault, a TDI Technical Instructor and PADI Technical Instructor Trainer, Rimstone delivers comprehensive training across the entire spectrum of open and closed circuit technical diving. Operating out of Fort White, Florida—the epicenter of Cave Country—our programs focus strictly on foundational stability, equipment fluency, and sharp analytical judgment.

Our training tracks support your entire progression: from your first steps into redundant technical setups and open-circuit decompression diving, through advanced mixed-gas trimix plans, to cave diving and unit-specific CCR transitions on the KISS Sidewinder and AP Inspiration platforms. We train thinking divers to excel in unforgiving environments, because in the end, skill is built one dive at a time.

The diver behind the training

Active diver. Obsessively prepared instructor.

Whether you are starting sidemount, pushing into cave, or stepping across to closed-circuit, we build every skill deliberately until it holds up under pressure. Every course is built around deliberate practice and the belief that true skill is built one dive at a time, focusing entirely on true peer-to-peer performance and long-term diving confidence.

FAQ

Common questions

Straight answers about locations, course length, prerequisites and booking.

Where are Rimstone courses taught?

Training is based in Fort White, Florida, in the heart of North Florida's Cave Country. Open-water, cavern and cave dives take place in the North Florida springs, including Ginnie Springs, Little River, Peacock Springs and Madison Blue Spring. Cave guiding is also offered in the Riviera Maya cenotes near Tulum and Playa del Carmen, Mexico.

Which certification agencies do you teach?

Courses follow TDI (Technical Diving International) and PADI Tec Rec pathways. Tim is a TDI Technical Instructor and a PADI Technical Instructor Trainer.

How long does a sidemount course take?

Sidemount training typically takes 2 to 3 days. You need at least an Open Water certification, comfortable core buoyancy skills and to be medically fit to dive.

How long does it take to become a cave diver?

Cave training runs in three stages: Cavern Diver (about 2 to 3 days), Intro to Cave Diver (about 2 to 3 days) and Full Cave Diver (about 4 to 5 days). In total, expect roughly 5 to 10 days of training depending on your starting skills.

What do I need before starting cave diving training?

You should have solid buoyancy and trim, logged open-water experience and be medically fit to dive. A Nitrox certification is recommended.

How long do technical diving courses take?

Open-circuit technical courses typically take 4 to 6 days per level. The track runs from Technical Foundations (PADI Tec Basics / TDI Intro to Tech) through decompression diving to mixed gas and trimix. You need Advanced Open Water and Nitrox certifications to start.

Which rebreathers can I train on?

CCR courses are taught on the KISS Sidewinder and the AP Inspiration, so you train on the unit you intend to dive. Cave-specific CCR courses are open to divers on any active CCR platform.

Can I try sidemount or a rebreather before signing up for a course?

Yes. A 1-day technical demo lets you get hands-on with sidemount, doubles and closed-circuit rebreather configurations before you commit to a full course.

Do I need a medical form?

Yes. Every diver completes the diver medical questionnaire before any in-water training. You can download it from the website.

How do I book a course?

Email tim@rimstonediving.com or call, text or WhatsApp +1 (206) 227-9715. Office hours are Monday to Friday, 9:00 to 5:00 Eastern Time.

Not sure where to start?

Book a 1-day technical demo and get hands-on with sidemount, doubles and closed-circuit configurations before you commit to a full course.
